added_failures_note: unmeasured: the reviewed manifest names no base gate log, so the added-failure count was not taken

findings.text: follow-on: the supervisor string re-implements a bounded exponential restart back-off that the repository already owns as fleet_supervisor.next_backoff (reckon/crew/fleet_supervisor.py:539, applied by session_host at session_host.py:494); the inline curve (0.1 s doubling to a 0.8 s cap) and its five-crash bound now sit beside that owner and can drift from it, and reuse was possible because the producer argv already resolves the reckon console script.

follow-on: the bound counts every crash over the supervisor's entire lifetime and never resets after a steady run, so "a producer that keeps crashing" is not what it measures — a producer that runs healthily for days and then crashes five times is abandoned, whereas the shared fleet_supervisor.next_backoff resets its delay after a steady run (fleet_supervisor.py:539).

follow-on: the no-restart-on-zero case is exercised by a plain `return` from the watch loop rather than an expiring lease, so the test bit that stands for "a lease that expired exits zero" is an ordinary clean exit; the exit-status behaviour under test is the same, but the case does not cover the lease-expiry path the plan names.

follow-on: the manifest records baseline_suite as the prose "none — the new focused test file does not exist at the base revision" although a base-arm log does exist at first-gate.log (revision aaab0bca, 5 passed 1 failed), so the added-failure count derives as unmeasured and neither arm's delta can be checked against the other.
